title: Making money 1 year later
description: Making money 1 year later. How to make money easy // 8 year old kid shows you how he makes money. The SportTastic kid is awesome, makes it look easy to earn money. in this video you will learn how to make easy money. Follow this kid as he makes easy cash. Just fun and making money, Amir rocks.

asr.full_text: What's up guys? I got something special today. I've been a youtuber for one year! I want to thank you guys for believing in me, subscribing, and watching my videos. I have 16,143 subscribers as of today. You guys remember how to make money as a kid? Well, I'm still doing it. Well, I have four bags and it should equal more money. Hey you guys, we're finna go and drop these off. You should watch my first video and click this link. Over time I've been earning money. As you can see. Hey, wait a minute, subscribe to my videos. I need more subscribers. Oh yeah, don't forget to hit the like button and turn on the notification bell. I got a tip for you guys. You guys know how I recycle bottles? If you recycle glass, you get way more money. I'm only 8 years old. Imagine when I turn 18 how much money I will have earned. I'm going to pay off my college. Might even buy a new car. You can do whatever you want to with it. You can do dances like I just did. Start your own business. Give your money away to people. I'm just here to tell you that it does work. This year, I'm going to try to find more ways to make money. So me and you can get rich. But you gotta be along for the ride, subscriber. Wink wink. As I said last year, the earth is getting a little cleaner, but also my pocket is getting. A little greener. Until next time, the Sportastic Kids signing out.

textual.observation: The speaker presents recycling glass bottles and dropping off collected bags as a way to earn more money.

evidence.quote: Hey you guys, we're finna go and drop these off.
If you recycle glass, you get way more money.

textual.context: Presented as the speaker's personal recycling activity and money-making explanation; the records do not establish whether the claim is being promoted commercially or discussed as an example.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised monetary return is linked to the requested activity of recycling glass and dropping off collected bottles, which may require later assessment of the stated payment conditions.
textual.limitations: The records do not state the payment amount, recipient, redemption process, fees, or whether the activity produced the claimed return.

textual.observation: The speaker asks viewers to subscribe while linking subscriber participation with becoming rich.

evidence.quote: So me and you can get rich.
But you gotta be along for the ride, subscriber.

textual.context: The request appears in a video-audience engagement context and may be rhetorical or promotional; the records do not clarify whether subscribing is presented as a condition for receiving money.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised wealth outcome is presented in connection with becoming a subscriber, creating a reward-and-action relationship requiring later context assessment.
textual.limitations: No payment, transfer, recruitment structure, eligibility condition, or specific benefit for subscribers is described.

textual_context_notes.observation: The money-making claims are attributed to the speaker's own experience and are presented by a self-described eight-year-old.

evidence.quote: I've been a youtuber for one year!
I'm just here to tell you that it does work.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it shows a personal demonstration of collecting and recycling items as a way to make money, without a stated fee, investment request, or commercial payment flow for viewers. References to getting rich are paired with requests for subscriptions, likes, and notifications rather than financial participation, and the cash shown does not by itself establish deception.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The main content is a personal money-making account centered on collecting and recycling bottles, with a general tip about glass, rather than a structured earning service or investment offer.
